findings.title: Eastern District of Virginia - 'Bulletproof' website domain seized in international law enforcement operation
findings.summary_md: On October 27, 2026, the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Eastern District of Virginia and the FBI Washington Field Office announced the court-authorized seizure of virtualine.net. The site was used for prolific criminal activity, including advertising sexually explicit images of minors, ransomware, and cryptocurrency laundering. Authorities said Virtualine knowingly hosted a forum distributing CSAM and ignored repeated notices from NCMEC, law enforcement, and a victim's attorney.

findings.title: FBI Seizes Virtualine Domain After Provider Led Bulletproof Hosting Sector in Illicit Inflows - TRM Labs
findings.summary_md: TRM Labs reported that on 27 October 2026 the FBI seized the domain of Virtualine, a Russian-speaking bulletproof hosting provider. The firm noted Virtualine received the most illicit-attributed value in 2026 to date among tracked bulletproof hosts, with a Russian drug marketplace accounting for roughly 44% of direct payments, a sextortion scheme for nearly 17%, a cryptocurrency mixer for almost 13%, ransomware for nearly 5%, and malware for 2%.

findings.title: International Law Enforcement Seizes Virtualine Bulletproof Hosting - Chainalysis
findings.summary_md: Chainalysis reported the October 27, 2026 seizure of virtualine.net, describing Virtualine as a bulletproof hosting service marketed on cybercrime forums that accepted direct bitcoin payments through unhosted wallet addresses. The service operated under aliases Secury, Massgod, Spamhouse, Lanedo, and Omegatech, and promised to shield customers from law enforcement and abuse complaints.
